minutes.headline: Agricultural Commission voted to recommend Mary Ray Holman for the planning board's economic development committee.
minutes.summary: The commission met remotely. It discussed a court ruling treating dog breeding as agricultural, then planned a farm brochure with a graphic designer who joined the meeting. It voted to recommend a member for the economic development committee and heard an update on the signature process for a public market. It agreed to send an earlier letter to several town offices, then adjourned.

votes.motion: Recommend Mary Ray Holman to the planning board for the economic development committee position

budget_items.what_was_said: The commission offered to give the designer something for his services. He said it was for a good cause and they would work something out.
A member planned to look into state agricultural grants, noting the commission got one earlier for signs.
The designer said per-copy printing cost falls as quantity rises, and expected a total of a couple hundred dollars.
The commission said it needs to work out what is in its account. It has no income apart from the market and no budget line, and members said they should push for one.
A member noted a bond bill is waiting for a community kitchen application.

decisions.decision: Members will split up the farm list and contact farms. A blast email to farmers will be sent to gauge willingness to be in the brochure, with phone calls to those who do not reply.
The commission's earlier letter will go to animal control, the police chief, the select board, the board of health and the fire chief. The chair will send it.
The farmers market recap and plans will go on the next meeting agenda.
The chair will report the recommendation to the planning board to be put on its agenda.

what_happened.line: The Agricultural Commission voted to recommend Mary Ray Holman to the planning board for the economic development committee position.
Members agreed to split the farm list, send a blast email to farmers, and phone those who do not reply, to gauge interest in a farm brochure.
The commission will send its earlier letter to animal control, the police chief, the select board, the board of health and the fire chief.
The commission said it has no budget line and no income apart from the market, and members said they should push for one.
The farmers market recap and plans will go on the next meeting agenda.

why_it_matters: The commission pays for its brochure and other work from an account it has not yet tallied and that has no budget line, so any funding would have to come from grants or a future town appropriation that residents may be asked to vote on.
The recommended committee seat feeds into the planning board's economic development work, which can affect how farmland and agricultural businesses are treated in town planning.
watch_next: The chair will report the recommendation to the planning board to be placed on its agenda.
The farmers market recap and plans are due on the commission's next meeting agenda.
